pr_title: Fix issue with Get-Process -Module failing to stop when piped to Select-Object
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Previously when running `Get-Process -Module` and piping to `Select-Object`, you would receive this error:

![getmodule-error](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20082136/123678048-2783cb80-d889-11eb-96f0-be44e0a4f2e7.PNG)

Where the command succeeds, but the upstream output is not halted and the `Get-Process: Cannot enumerate the modules of the "pwsh" process.` non-terminating error is included. 

To fix this, I added another clause to catch [`PipelineStoppedException`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.management.automation.pipelinestoppedexception?view=powershellsdk-7.0.0) from `WriteObject`, and rethrow error, which omits the error message completely. 

![getmodule-error-fix](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20082136/123678491-b2fd5c80-d889-11eb-9faa-bea08c89a7ad.PNG)

Also added a Pester test to verify this.

Fix #15117

issue_context.title: Get-Process -Module fails to stop when piped to Select-Object -First
issue_context.body:
It seems that when `Select-Object -First` tries to stop upstream pipeline input, `Get-Process -Module` doesn't handle this request properly and emits many spurious error messages.

## Steps to reproduce

```powershell
Get-Process -Module  -Id $PID -ev errs | Select-Object -First 1 
$errs.Count | Should -Be 0
```

## Expected behavior

No errors should occur, and the test should succeed.

## Actual behavior

Error message `Get-Process: Cannot enumerate the modules of the "pwsh" process.` is (wrongly) emitted (without `Select-Object -First`, the command succeeds), and the test fails:

```none
InvalidResult: Expected 0, but got 1.
```

## Environment data

```none
PowerShell Core 7.2.0-preview.4
```
comments:
Problem is here:

https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/be7d36603d1cc60abd4e8e738ead8f437b7869fa/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management/commands/management/Process.cs#L591-L630

Either the scope of the `try` needs to not include `WriteObject`, or another clause for `FlowControlException` should be added that rethrows.

review_comments: I guess we will see the same for any collection/enumeration. If so would a fix be in WriteObject() method?

I think that since we have to catch errors from WriteObject() here anyway and make them non-terminating so we can enumerate a process's modules, "fixing" this in WriteObject() itself would just give us the same issue in this cmdlet.

I'm almost positive that rethrowing a PipelineStoppedException is something WriteObject() is already doing here.

Yeah I'm not sure of a better way to do this, catching `PipelineStoppedException` then rethrowing will stop the whole pipeline and avoid writing the non-terminating error. 

Seems like other places in the code doing this well to handle Select-Object:

https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/658837323599ab1c7a81fe66fcd43f7420e4402b/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/InternalCommands.cs#L770-L774

I'm open to suggestions if there is a nicer way to do this 🙂
Uh, there doesn't seem to be a common solution.
